Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team liked the latency profile and fallback behavior. Leadership wants to move to a small Dedicated pilot to validate inference economics and reliability for our most-used endpoint (clinical triage assistant). Before we lock timelines, procurement asked what you need from us to size the Dedicated fleet and confirm a rough cost.

Can you confirm the exact telemetry / sample data you need? We can export logs but want to avoid heavy work. Off the top of my head: average requests per minute, peak 5m QPS, prompt/response sizes, concurrency per session, sample payloads. Is there a template you prefer?

Also — target p99 latency: 200ms for short queries, but we can accept softer for longer responses. We'll also include a procurement contact in case contract timing changes.

Hi Samantha — great to connect. Appreciate the clarity on p99 targets. To make sizing quick and accurate, we prefer a small CSV export and a couple of notes — I'm attaching a short template we use (session_imprint_template.xlsx). If you can populate the CSV columns below it will be ideal:

- timestamp (UTC)
- endpoint (API route or logical feature name)
- session_id (or anonymous user id)
- prompt_tokens (int)
- response_tokens (int)
- total_latency_ms
- outcome_tag (optional: success/timeout/error)

If you can't export every field, start with endpoint, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, and timestamp for a 48–72 hour sample that includes one known peak day if possible. The more realistic the sample (including retry spikes or bot traffic) the better for us.

Two internal asks for you:
1) Which region do you plan to deploy in (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1)?
2) Do you expect warm sessions (multi-request dialogues) or mostly stateless single-call requests?

I'll loop in our Solutions Architect to recommend default GPU SKUs and an initial occupancy estimate once we see the sample.

Best,
Lauren Bishop

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Samantha's note. Can you review and add any required telemetry fields before I send the template? They mentioned p99 ~200ms for short queries and will provide a pick of sample days.

Karthik — we should ask for:
- session length distribution (count of requests per session) so we can size KV cache and session pooling,
- token histogram broken into prompt bins (0-32, 33-128, 129-512, 513+),
- top 10 endpoints by QPS,
- hourly dayparting for 7 days if possible (shows burst windows),
- retry/backoff patterns (so we can model transient spikes),
- any authentication middleware that enriches payloads (affects overall payload size).

Marissa — pricing note: early pilot we can provide a conservative occupancy estimate and a 30-day reserved pilot config; if they commit to a 6mo+ contract we recommend SKU mix change and add burst capacity. I'll need a quick sanity check on suggested GPU mix after Karthik's sizing.

Hi Samantha — following up with a slightly expanded template and a short checklist so we can return an initial Dedicated sizing within 48 hours of receiving sample data. Attached: session_imprint_template.xlsx (columns pre-filled) and a small example CSV (vero_token_sample.csv) that shows the exact header mapping.

What we need (minimal viable sample):
- 48–72 hour CSV with columns: timestamp_utc, endpoint, session_id, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, total_latency_ms, is_streaming (true/false), aux_payload_size_bytes (int), outcome_tag
- Annotate one known peak window (approx start/end) so we can model burst amplification
- Indicate the region for deployment and approximate target p99 SLAs per endpoint (if different from the 200ms you mentioned)
- Any scheduled jobs or batch jobs that might create sustained background traffic

Why we ask for these fields:
- prompt/response token breakup lets us calculate token-economics per GPU and expected throughput.
- session_id + timestamp lets us estimate KV cache residency and session-affinity needs.
- is_streaming and aux payload bytes let us size network egress and streaming threads.
- dayparting/peak windows let us recommend burst pool size and oversubscription guardrails.

Next steps:
1) If you can drop the sample in this Drive folder (link) or reply with the CSV, we'll run the sizing and send a draft SKU mix + occupancy assumptions within 48 hours.
2) We can schedule a 30-minute call to review the recommendations and talk pilot timelines (suggested: 2–4 week pilot run).
